title: US Workers Name AI Skills as 'Career Currency'
paragraphs: More and more Americans believe that skills in artificial intelligence (AI) are becoming a valuable form of "career currency," according to a new survey.
The survey of 2,000 American adults was carried out by Talker Research for CSU Global, an online university. The results were released in early September.

The survey found that 57% of Americans view AI certifications as a kind of career currency, meaning they believe these qualifications can help them get ahead at work. Young people were especially likely to see AI as important. Around 65% of millennials and 64% of Gen Z respondents described AI's influence as career-changing.

When asked which skills are becoming more valuable at work, 18% chose knowing how to use AI. Other skills that respondents valued included problem-solving, adaptability, communication and critical thinking.

Many workers also expect AI to have an impact very soon. About two-thirds of working respondents said they expect AI to affect their career path within a year. Half said they believe every new employee will need good AI skills within six months.

However, many people do not yet feel ready for this change. While 48% had a positive view of AI in the workplace, the same percentage said they did not feel qualified to use it at work. Meanwhile, 62% of employed respondents said they would use AI more at work if they had more confidence, encouragement or training.

Dr. Audra Spicer, CSU Global's interim president and CEO, said the main barriers to using AI at work are gaps in employee confidence, company culture and training. She also said that educational opportunities and good leadership can help close these gaps.
It is worth noting, however, that the survey measured people's opinions. It does not show whether employers actually prefer to hire people with AI certifications.
